definitions.target_snapshot: Repository head/tree observed at discovery start. Later branch mutations must not alter the discovered checkpoint set for a snapshot-consistent strategy.
definitions.snapshot_inconsistent: Discovery combines repository states from different heads/trees.
definitions.phantom_omission: A checkpoint present in the target snapshot is missing from discovery.
definitions.phantom_addition: A checkpoint/incarnation absent from the target snapshot is included in discovery.
definitions.false_duplicate_selection: The strategy proceeds after discovering the same logical checkpoint twice across a moving-head restart/delete-recreate race.

findings: Multi-call discovery against moving main is not a snapshot: concurrent create/delete/delete-recreate and ref ABA can produce phantom omission/addition even when a start/end ref equality check returns to the same head.
Pinning one root tree SHA and following child tree SHAs preserves a single repository snapshot across head movement, response restart and application-level delete at newer heads in the tested model.

A one-shot recursive pinned-tree response is safe but may be incomplete when GitHub reports truncation; treating truncation as fail-closed is safe, while pinned non-recursive subtree traversal restores progress without changing snapshots.
Merkle/prefix summary caches are safe only as verified accelerators bound to a source tree SHA; stale/missing summaries must fall back to the pinned tree rather than become authority.
Snapshot consistency does not replace semantic authority fencing: every selector must revalidate the current authority after discovery and before LATEST selection.
